conditions: Applies to Boolean assertion expressions and the stlx interpreter described in Snyder’s dated report.
limitations: The report’s description of the three assertion behaviors and its separate command-line argument list have different scopes.
The cited passages leave the selection mechanism for skipping all assertions and any default assertion state unresolved. No claim is made about later implementations.

triggers: Reevaluate source corrections, revised applicability, or material contrary evidence.

statement: Snyder’s 1990 SETL2 reference describes three assertion behaviors in its historical interpreter. It can skip all assertions, or stop on a failing assertion while either skipping or logging successful assertions. The operation manual lists two explicit stlx -a values, f for skipping successful assertions and l for logging them.
